The Yuma Library District is in **Arizona**.  
Arizona’s second‑largest city by population is **Tucson**.

From official climatological records, Tucson’s wettest year was **1905**, when the city recorded **24.2 inches (24.17 inches)** of total precipitation—well above its typical annual average.  

**Sources**

- National Weather Service “Tucson all‑time extremes” page lists 24.17 inches in 1905 as the wettest year.  
- Extreme Weather Watch’s “Most Yearly Precipitation in Tucson History” page confirms 24.2 inches in 1905 as the record.

steps.text:
The Yuma Library District is in **Arizona**.  
Arizona’s second‑largest city by population is **Tucson**.

From official climatological records, Tucson’s wettest year was **1905**, when the city recorded **24.2 inches (24.17 inches)** of total precipitation—well above its typical annual average.  

**Sources**

- National Weather Service “Tucson all‑time extremes” page lists 24.17 inches in 1905 as the wettest year.  
- Extreme Weather Watch’s “Most Yearly Precipitation in Tucson History” page confirms 24.2 inches in 1905 as the record.
